items.title: The two-particle exchange operator and the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), let
$H\widehat\otimes H$ be its completed tensor square with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and for $n=2$ let
$(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_2}$ and the projections $P_\pm^{(2)}$ be those of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Write
$\tau:=U_{(12)}$ for the **exchange operator**, so that
$\tau\bigl(\kappa(u\otimes v)\bigr)=\kappa(v\otimes u)$ for $u,v\in H$; in the
sequel the inclusion is suppressed and $u\otimes v$ denotes
$\kappa(u\otimes v)$. Then:

(a) $\tau$ is self-adjoint and $\tau^2=I$; consequently $\tau$ is an isometry
with $\tau^{-1}=\tau=\tau^{*}$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(b) $P_+^{(2)}=\tfrac12(I+\tau)$ and $P_-^{(2)}=\tfrac12(I-\tau)$, and
$$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(2)}=\{x\in H\widehat\otimes H:\tau x=x\},\qquad \operatorname{ran}P_-^{(2)}=\{x\in H\widehat\otimes H:\tau x=-x\};$$

(c) for all $u,v\in H$,
$$\|u\otimes v+v\otimes u\|^{2}=2\bigl(\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}+|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}\bigr), \qquad \|u\otimes v-v\otimes u\|^{2}=2\bigl(\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}-|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}\bigr);$$
in particular, if $u,v$ are orthonormal, then
$s:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(u\otimes v+v\otimes u)$ and
$a:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(u\otimes v-v\otimes u)$ are orthonormal, $\tau s=s$ and
$\tau a=-a$, and both $\operatorname{ran}P_\pm^{(2)}$ are nonzero;

(d) whenever $u,v\in H$ are orthonormal,
$\tau\kappa(u\otimes v)\ne\kappa(u\otimes v)$. Consequently, if $H$
contains an orthonormal pair (equivalently, $\dim H\ge2$), both exchange
eigenspaces contain nonzero vectors and $\tau\ne I$. If $H=\{0\}$ or
$\dim H=1$, then $\tau=I$, $P_+^{(2)}=I$ and $P_-^{(2)}=0$; for $H=\{0\}$
the tensor square and both ranges are zero.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The complex Hilbert space $H$ with inner product linear in the first argument, the completed tensor square $H\widehat\otimes H$ with inclusion $\kappa$, the permutation unitaries $U_\pi$ for $n=2$ and the projections $P_\pm^{(2)}$, and vectors $u,v\in H$.

[F1] **Tensor square.** $\kappa:H\odot H\to H\widehat\otimes H$ is a linear isometry with dense image, $\kappa(u\otimes v)$ is bilinear in $(u,v)$, $\|\kappa(u\otimes v)\|=\|u\|\,\|v\|$ and $\langle\kappa(u\otimes v),\kappa(u'\otimes v')\rangle=\langle u,u'\rangle\langle v,v'\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (a)-(d), [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]).

[F2] **Permutation unitaries.** $U_{(12)}\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes H)$ is the unique bounded operator with $U_{(12)}\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa(v\otimes u)$; it is unitary with $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$ and $U_\pi^{*}=U_{\pi^{-1}}$. For every $\pi\in S_2$, $U_\pi P_+^{(2)}=P_+^{(2)}U_\pi=P_+^{(2)}$ and $U_\pi P_-^{(2)}=P_-^{(2)}U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-^{(2)}$. The orthogonal projections are $P_+^{(2)}=\frac12\sum_{\pi\in S_2}U_\pi$ and $P_-^{(2)}=\frac12\sum_{\pi\in S_2}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (a)-(c), [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F3] **Orthogonal projections.** An orthogonal projection $P$ satisfies $P^2=P=P^{*}$, and its range is a closed subspace ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]).

[F4] **Adjoint and operator norm.** For $T\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes H)$ the Hilbert adjoint $T^{*}$ is the unique bounded operator with $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,T^{*}y\rangle$, and $T$ is an isometry exactly when $T^{*}T=I$; $\|Tx\|\le\|T\|\,\|x\|$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], [[def-operator-norm]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

## Proof

1.1 [The exchange operator is a self-adjoint involution] By [F2] with $\pi=\sigma=(12)$ one has $\tau^2=U_{(12)(12)}=U_e=I$, and $\tau^{*}=U_{(12)^{-1}}=U_{(12)}=\tau$; hence $\tau^{-1}=\tau=\tau^{*}$ and $\tau$ is an isometry, which is (a). [F2, F4, algebra]

1.2 [The projections in terms of the exchange operator] Since $S_2=\{e,(12)\}$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(e)=1$, $\operatorname{sgn}((12))=-1$, the formulas of [F2] give $P_+^{(2)}=\frac12(U_e+U_{(12)})=\frac12(I+\tau)$ and $P_-^{(2)}=\frac12(U_e-U_{(12)})=\frac12(I-\tau)$, which is the first assertion of (b). [F2, algebra]

2.1 [Eigenspaces as ranges] Let $x\in H\widehat\otimes H$. If $\tau x=x$, then $\frac12(I+\tau)x=x$, so $x\in\operatorname{ran}\frac12(I+\tau)$; conversely if $x=\frac12(I+\tau)y$ for some $y$, then $\tau x=\frac12(\tau y+\tau^2y)=\frac12(\tau y+y)=x$ by step 1.1. Hence the fixed space of $\tau$ is $\operatorname{ran}\frac12(I+\tau)=\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(2)}$ by step 1.2; the same substitution with $x=\frac12(I-\tau)y$ gives $\tau x=-x$, and conversely $\tau x=-x$ implies $x=\frac12(I-\tau)x$, so the $(-1)$-eigenspace is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(2)}$. This completes (b). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F3, algebra]

2.2 [Norm identities on products] By [F1] the elementary tensors satisfy $\|u\otimes v\|^{2}=\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}$ and $\langle u\otimes v,v\otimes u\rangle=\langle u,v\rangle\langle v,u\rangle=|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}$; expanding $\|u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u\|^{2}=\|u\otimes v\|^{2}+\|v\otimes u\|^{2}\pm2\operatorname{Re}\langle u\otimes v,v\otimes u\rangle$ and using that the last number is the real number $|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}$ gives the two identities of (c). If $u,v$ are orthonormal then $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=0$, so $s$ and $a$ have norm one; moreover $\tau s=\frac1{\sqrt2}(v\otimes u+u\otimes v)=s$ and $\tau a=\frac1{\sqrt2}(v\otimes u-u\otimes v)=-a$ by [F2]; and $\langle s,a\rangle=\frac12(\|u\otimes v\|^{2}-\|v\otimes u\|^{2})=0$, so $s,a$ are orthonormal and $s\ne0\ne a$. This proves (c). [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Nonvanishing of the swapped product] Let $u,v$ be orthonormal. Then $u\otimes v$ and $v\otimes u$ are orthonormal in $H\widehat\otimes H$: both have norm one by [F1], and $\langle u\otimes v,v\otimes u\rangle=\langle u,v\rangle\langle v,u\rangle=0$. Hence $v\otimes u\ne u\otimes v$, so $\tau(u\otimes v)\ne u\otimes v$ by [F2]; taking $x:=u\otimes v$ and $x':=s$ and $x'':=a$ from step 2.2 gives nonzero vectors with $\tau x'=x'$ and $\tau x''=-x''$, so $\tau\ne I$. This proves (d). [F1, F2, step 2.2, algebra, construct]

4.1 [Zero and one-dimensional spaces] If $H=\{0\}$, all elementary tensors are zero and their completion is zero, so $\tau=I$ on that space. If $H$ is one-dimensional, fix a unit spanning vector $e$. Every elementary tensor has the form $(\alpha e)\otimes(\beta e)=\alpha\beta(e\otimes e)$ and its swap is $\beta\alpha(e\otimes e)$, the same vector. Hence $\tau=I$ on the dense algebraic tensor space and, by boundedness, on its completion. Step 1.2 then gives $P_+^{(2)}=I$ and $P_-^{(2)}=0$ in both cases. If $\dim H\ge2$, normalize a nonzero vector $u$ and choose $w$ outside its span; the nonzero vector $w-\langle w,u\rangle u$ normalizes to a unit $v$ orthogonal to $u$, so step 3.1 applies. This proves all branches of (d). [F1, F2, step 1.2, step 3.1, choose, algebra]

5.1 [Assembly] Step 1.1 proves (a), steps 1.2 and 2.1 prove (b), step 2.2 proves (c) and steps 3.1 and 4.1 prove (d). Only the cited tensor and permutation mathematics and the Countable Choice hypothesis of [F2] were used; no physical reading of the exchange operator is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the letter $\tau$.** The operator is the $n=2$ instance of the
  permutation unitaries; the notation $\tau$ matches the exchange operator of
  the source treatments and is used on this pair's pages for the two-particle
  swap.
- **Scope.** The lemma concerns a single Hilbert space and its tensor square;
  it asserts nothing about particles, spin, statistics or dynamics. The
  physical reading of $\tau$ as the exchange of two labelled factors is fixed
  in [[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
  on the page for the identical-particle model.

items.title: Slater and symmetric occupation-number bases of the finite-dimensional permutation sectors
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Let
$H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold completed tensor power with
$H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let
$P_\pm^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$, be the permutation
projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. For a
multi-index $i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$ write
$$e_i:=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\}\ (j=1,\dots,d).$$
For $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ with $|J|=n$, written $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_n\}$, put
$$e_J^\wedge:=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, e_{j_{\sigma(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\sigma(n)}},$$
and for $\lambda\in W(n,d):=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ put
$\operatorname{orb}(\lambda):=\{c\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n:|c|=\lambda\}$ and
$m_\lambda:=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$. Then:

(a) *product basis*: $(e_i)_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$H^{\otimes n}$, and $\dim H^{\otimes n}=d^n$;

(b) *Slater basis*: for every $J$ with $|J|=n$ one has
$e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})$ and the
family $(e_J^\wedge)_{J\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal family whose
closed linear span is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$; it is therefore an
orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$,
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$, and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ when $n>d$. Moreover for every multi-index
$i$ one has $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ when two entries of $i$ coincide, and
$$P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\,\frac{e_J^\wedge}{\sqrt{n!}}$$
when the entries of $i$ are pairwise distinct with underlying set $J$ and
$\rho_i\in S_n$ is the unique permutation with $i_k=j_{\rho_i(k)}$;

(c) *symmetric basis*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the vector $m_\lambda$ is
nonzero, the family $(m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in W(n,d)}$ is orthogonal,
$U_\pi m_\lambda=m_\lambda$ for every $\pi\in S_n$, and for every multi-index
$i$ there is a real number $\gamma_i>0$ with
$P_+^{(n)}(e_i)=\gamma_i\,m_{|i|}$; consequently
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is the linear span of $(m_\lambda)$, the family
$(m_\lambda)$ is an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$;

(d) *occupation operators*: for $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ the map
$$N_j:H^{\otimes n}\to H^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,e_i\rangle\,e_i,$$
is a self-adjoint bounded endomorphism, the $N_j$ commute pairwise,
$\sum_{j=1}^dN_j=nI$, and
$$N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)\,e_J^\wedge,\qquad N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_j\,m_\lambda .$$
Consequently both sectors are invariant under every $N_j$, the joint
eigenspaces of $(N_1,\dots,N_d)$ inside $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$ are the
lines $\mathbb Ce_J^\wedge$ (one for each $n$-element subset $J$, with
eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$), and the joint eigenspaces inside
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ are the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ (one for each
$\lambda\in W(n,d)$, with eigenvalue vector $\lambda$).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$ of dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis $(e_1,\dots,e_d)$, the tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ with permutation projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$, multi-indices $i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$, subsets $J$ with $|J|=n$, and $\lambda\in W(n,d)$.

[F1] **Tensor powers.** For all $n$ the tensor power carries bilinear elementary tensors $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$ with $\|v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\|=\|v_1\|\cdots\|v_n\|$ and $\langle v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n,w_1\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n\rangle=\prod_k\langle v_k,w_k\rangle$; for orthonormal families $(f_a)_{a\in A}$ in $H$ and $(g_b)_{b\in B}$ in $K$ with dense spans, the products $f_a\otimes g_b$ form an orthonormal family in $H\widehat\otimes K$ with dense span; the algebraic tensor product is dense in each completion ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (b)-(d)).

[F2] **Permutation projections.** $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)}$ defines unitaries with $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$ and $U_\pi^{*}=U_{\pi^{-1}}$; $P_+^{(n)}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi$ and $P_-^{(n)}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$ are orthogonal projections with $U_\pi P_-^{(n)}=P_-^{(n)}U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-^{(n)}$, and $P_-^{(n)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=0$ whenever two of the vectors $v_k$ coincide ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (a),(c),(d)).

[F3] **Determinant.** For a square matrix $A=(a_{ab})$ of size $n$ over a commutative ring, $\det(A)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{a=1}^n a_{\sigma(a),a}$; in particular $\det(I_n)=1$, and $\det(A)=0$ if some row of $A$ is zero ([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]).

[F4] **Binomial coefficients as counts.** $\binom dk=|[d]^k|$ for $d,k\in\mathbb N$, so with $k=n$ the number of $n$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,d\}$ is $\binom dn$ ([[def-binomial-coefficient]]).

[F5] **Weak compositions.** For $m\ge1$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, $|W(n,m)|=\binom{n+m-1}{m-1}$ ([[thm-stars-and-bars]]); and $\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$ ([[thm-binomial-closed-formula]] clause 3, with $N=n+d-1$ and $k=d-1$).

[F6] **Orthonormal expansions.** For an orthonormal family $(f_a)_{a\in A}$ in a Hilbert space whose closed linear span is the whole space, every $x$ equals the limit of the finite partial sums $\sum_{a\in F}\langle x,f_a\rangle f_a$; for a finite complete orthonormal family this is the finite equality $x=\sum_a\langle x,f_a\rangle f_a$ ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]] clauses 1 and 4, [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).

[F7] **Self-adjointness and boundedness.** A bounded endomorphism $T$ of $H^{\otimes n}$ is self-adjoint when $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle$ for all $x,y$, equivalently $T^{*}=T$ for the Hilbert adjoint of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]] ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; build the product basis by induction from the tensor construction, determine the two permutation projections on basis vectors by explicit reindexing sums, evaluate the resulting orthonormality as a determinant, read the dimension counts off the index sets, and compute the occupation operators on the two resulting bases.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [Product basis] We show by induction on $n$ that $(e_i)_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal basis of $H^{\otimes n}$. For $n=1$ this is the hypothesis. If it holds for $n$, then by [F1] applied to the orthonormal basis $(e_i)_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ of $H^{\otimes n}$ and $(e_j)_{j\in\{1,\dots,d\}}$ of $H$, the products $e_i\otimes e_j$ form an orthonormal family with dense span in $H^{\otimes(n+1)}=H^{\otimes n}\widehat\otimes H$; this is the displayed family for $n+1$, and its span is $H^{\otimes(n+1)}$ because $H^{\otimes(n+1)}$ is finite dimensional, so a dense subspace is the whole space. Hence the family is an orthonormal basis, its cardinality is $d\cdot d^n=d^{n+1}$ and $\dim H^{\otimes n}=d^n$, which is (a). [F1, algebra, induction]

1.2 [The alternating projection on basis vectors] Let $i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$. By the action formula of [F2], $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)e_{i_{\pi^{-1}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_{\pi^{-1}(n)}}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\tau\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)e_{i_{\tau(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_{\tau(n)}}$ after the substitution $\tau=\pi^{-1}$. If two entries of $i$ coincide, say $i_k=i_l$ with $k\ne l$, then the transposition $\upsilon=(kl)$ satisfies $e_{i_{\upsilon\tau(1)}}\otimes\cdots=e_{i_{\tau(1)}}\otimes\cdots$ for every $\tau$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\upsilon\tau)=-\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)$, so the sum pairs to zero and $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ by [F2]. If the entries are pairwise distinct with underlying set $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_n\}$ and $i_k=j_{\rho_i(k)}$, then $e_{i_{\tau(1)}}\otimes\cdots=e_{j_{\rho_i\tau(1)}}\otimes\cdots$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i\tau)$; substituting $\omega=\rho_i\tau$ gives $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\frac{\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)}{n!}\sum_{\omega\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\omega)e_{j_{\omega(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\omega(n)}}=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\frac{e_J^\wedge}{\sqrt{n!}}$, which is the second formula of (b). [F2, algebra]

1.3 [Orthonormality of the Slater family] For subsets $J,K$ with $|J|=|K|=n$ put $A_{ab}:=\langle e_{j_a},e_{k_b}\rangle=\delta_{j_a,k_b}$. By [F1], $\langle e_J^\wedge,e_K^\wedge\rangle=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma,\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)\prod_{l=1}^n A_{\sigma(l),\pi(l)}$. For each fixed $\pi$ substitute $\sigma=\omega\pi$ and reindex the product by $t=\pi(l)$. Then $\prod_l A_{\sigma(l),\pi(l)}=\prod_t A_{\omega(t),t}$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\omega)$, so the sum over $\pi$ contributes $n!$ and the remaining sum is $\det(A)$ by [F3]. For $J=K$, $A=I_n$ and this is $1$; for $J\ne K$, some $j_a$ is absent from $K$, giving a zero row and determinant $0$. Thus the Slater family is orthonormal. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Occupation operators] For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ the formula of (d) defines a linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space $H^{\otimes n}$; by [F6] applied to the complete orthonormal family $(e_i)$ we have $x=\sum_i\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i$ and $N_jx=\sum_i|i|_j\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i$ for every $x$. Self-adjointness: for $x,y\in H^{\otimes n}$ the expansions give $\langle N_jx,y\rangle=\sum_i|i|_j\langle x,e_i\rangle\overline{\langle y,e_i\rangle}=\langle x,N_jy\rangle$ because the numbers $|i|_j$ are real, so $N_j$ is self-adjoint by [F7]; it is bounded because its range is spanned by the finitely many $e_i$ with eigenvalue at most $n$, and $\|N_jx\|\le n\|x\|$. The same computation on the basis vectors $e_i$, on which $N_j$ is diagonal with the real eigenvalues $|i|_j$, gives $N_jN_ke_i=|i|_k|i|_je_i=N_kN_je_i$ and $\sum_jN_je_i=\bigl(\sum_j|i|_j\bigr)e_i=ne_i$; since the $e_i$ form a basis by step 1.1 and both sides of each identity are linear, $N_jN_k=N_kN_j$ and $\sum_{j=1}^dN_j=nI$. This proves the operator statements of (d) except the two eigenvector formulas. [F6, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Slater basis and its dimension] By step 1.2 each $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})$ lies in $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$, and each $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)$ is either zero or a multiple of some $e_J^\wedge$; since the $e_i$ form a basis of $H^{\otimes n}$ by step 1.1 and $P_-^{(n)}$ is linear, the closed linear span of $(e_J^\wedge)$ is exactly $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$ (a finite-dimensional, hence closed, subspace). By step 1.3 the family is orthonormal, so it is an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$, indexed by the $n$-element subsets $J$ of $\{1,\dots,d\}$; by [F4] there are $\binom dn$ of them, so $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$. If $n>d$, then two of the $n$ entries of any $i$ coincide, so $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ for every basis vector $e_i$ by step 1.2, whence $P_-^{(n)}=0$ and $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$. In particular $e_J^\wedge\ne0$ whenever $|J|=n\le d$. This completes (b). [F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

2.3 [The symmetric sums] Fix $\lambda\in W(n,d)$. The word $c$ that lists $1$ with multiplicity $\lambda_1$, then $2$ with multiplicity $\lambda_2$, and so on through $d$ has $|c|=\lambda$, so $\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)\ne\varnothing$ and $m_\lambda=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$ is a nonempty sum of orthonormal vectors of $H^{\otimes n}$, hence nonzero, with $\|m_\lambda\|^2=|\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)|$ by the orthonormality of the product basis in step 1.1 [F1]. If $\lambda\ne\mu$ then a word has a unique multiplicity vector, so $\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)\cap\operatorname{orb}(\mu)=\varnothing$ and the inner product of $m_\lambda$ and $m_\mu$ is the empty sum $0$. For $\pi\in S_n$ the map $c\mapsto\pi\cdot c$, $(\pi\cdot c)_k:=c_{\pi^{-1}(k)}$, permutes $\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)$ and $U_\pi e_c=e_{\pi\cdot c}$ by [F2], so $U_\pi m_\lambda=m_\lambda$. Finally, $P_+^{(n)}e_i=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}e_{\pi\cdot i}$ has coefficients supported on $\operatorname{orb}(|i|)$; for $c\in\operatorname{orb}(|i|)$ the set $\{\pi:\pi\cdot i=c\}$ is the coset $\pi_0\operatorname{Stab}(i)$ for any $\pi_0$ with $\pi_0\cdot i=c$, hence has cardinality $|\operatorname{Stab}(i)|\ge1$, and it is empty for $c\notin\operatorname{orb}(|i|)$; therefore $P_+^{(n)}e_i=\gamma_i\,m_{|i|}$ with $\gamma_i:=|\operatorname{Stab}(i)|/n!>0$. This proves all the assertions of (c) except the dimension. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Symmetric basis and its dimension] By step 2.3 the $m_\lambda$ are nonzero, pairwise orthogonal and lie in $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ (indeed $m_\lambda=\gamma_i^{-1}P_+^{(n)}e_i$ for any multi-index $i$ with $|i|=\lambda$, and such $i$ exists because $\lambda\in W(n,d)$); conversely every $P_+^{(n)}e_i$ is a multiple of some $m_\lambda$, so by linearity and the basis property of the $e_i$ the span of $(m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in W(n,d)}$ is $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$. A pairwise orthogonal family of nonzero vectors spanning a finite-dimensional space is a basis, so $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=|W(n,d)|=\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$ by [F5]. This completes (c). [F5, step 2.3, algebra]

4.1 [Occupation numbers on the two bases] Every summand $e_c$ of $e_J^\wedge$ has exactly one entry equal to $j$ when $j\in J$ and none otherwise, so $|c|_j=\mathbf 1_J(j)$ for every such $c$; and every $c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)$ has $|c|_j=\lambda_j$. Since the $N_j$ are linear and act diagonally on the $e_c$ by the formula of step 2.1, this gives $N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)e_J^\wedge$ and $N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_jm_\lambda$, the remaining assertions of (d). Both basis families displayed in (b) and (c) therefore consist of joint eigenvectors of $(N_1,\dots,N_d)$, and the two maps $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ and $\lambda\mapsto\lambda$ are injective; hence the joint eigenspaces inside the two sectors are the lines spanned by the corresponding basis vectors, as asserted in (d), and each sector is invariant under every $N_j$. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Assembly] Step 1.1 proves (a), steps 1.2, 1.3 and 2.2 prove (b), steps 2.3 and 3.1 prove (c), and steps 2.1 and 4.1 prove (d). The proof uses only the completed tensor powers, the permutation projections, the orthonormal expansions and the stated counting facts, under the Countable Choice hypothesis of [F1] and [F2]; no physical reading of the sectors or of the occupation operators is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.1, step 2.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Reading of the operators.** $N_j$ counts the particles occupying the
  declared basis vector $e_j$; the theorem proves the exact statements that
  the two permutation sectors diagonalise the family $(N_1,\dots,N_d)$ and
  that the antisymmetric sector has only the occupation values $0$ and $1$.
  The physical reading of this diagonalisation as an occupation readout of the
  framework belongs to
  [[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] and
  [[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]].
- **Finite dimension.** The dimension of $H$ is finite and is part of the
  hypotheses; no infinite-dimensional Slater basis or occupation operator is
  constructed here. The open case is treated by different machinery on the
  Fock-space pair.

items.title: Finite-mode occupation configurations: fermionic exclusion counts, bosonic counts and truncated dimensions
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $H^{\otimes n}$ and
$P_\pm^{(n)}$ be as in
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] (with
$P_\pm^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$), and let $W(n,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$
and $m_\lambda$ be the symmetric vectors of that theorem. Then:

(a) *fermionic configurations*: the map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection
from the set of $n$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,d\}$ onto the set
$\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$; consequently
$$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\#\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\textstyle\sum_j\lambda_j=n\},\qquad \sum_{n=0}^{d}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=2^{d};$$

(b) *bosonic configurations*: the assignment $\lambda\mapsto m_\lambda$ induces
a bijection from $W(n,d)$ onto the set of lines spanned by the orthogonal basis
$(m_\lambda)$, so the number of bosonic configurations of total occupation
exactly $n$ is $\binom{n+d-1}{n}=\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}$, and for every $N\ge0$ the
number of bosonic configurations of total occupation at most $N$ is
$$\sum_{n=0}^{N}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{N+d}{d};$$

(c) *exclusion counts*: no fermionic configuration has an entry $\ge2$, so the
antisymmetric Slater index set contains no $\lambda$ with $\lambda_j\ge2$ for
some $j$; for $n>d$ there is no fermionic configuration at all and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$, while for every $n$ and every $j$ the
bosonic configuration with $\lambda_j=n$ and all other entries $0$ occurs, so
no occupation bound holds in the symmetric sector;

(d) *consistency with the total occupation*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ one
has $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$, and for every fermionic configuration
$\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d\cap\{\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ likewise; in particular the
total occupation equals the particle number $n$ in both sectors.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$ of dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis $(e_1,\dots,e_d)$, the sectors $\operatorname{ran}P_\pm^{(n)}$ of the cited theorem, and $n,N\ge0$.

[F1] **Occupation basis.** The Slater vectors $e_J^\wedge$, $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ with $|J|=n$, form an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$, and $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$ with $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ for $n>d$; the symmetric vectors $(m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in W(n,d)}$ form an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$; each $e_J^\wedge$ has occupation vector $\mathbf 1_J$ and each $m_\lambda$ has occupation vector $\lambda$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (b),(c),(d)).

[F2] **Binomial counts and symmetry.** $\binom dn$ is the number of $n$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,d\}$ ([[def-binomial-coefficient]]), and $\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$ ([[thm-binomial-closed-formula]] clause 3, with $N=n+d-1$ and $k=d-1$).

[F3] **Weak compositions.** For $m\ge1$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, $|W(n,m)|=\binom{n+m-1}{m-1}$ ([[thm-stars-and-bars]]).

[F4] **Pascal rule and hockey stick.** For all $n,k\in\mathbb N$, $\binom{n+1}{k+1}=\binom nk+\binom n{k+1}$ and $\sum_{i<n+1}\binom ik=\binom{n+1}{k+1}$ as an $\mathbb N$-valued finite sum ([[thm-pascals-rule]]); the sector formula of the theorem is stated for the finite sums there defined.

[F5] **Row sum.** $\sum_{k<n+1}\binom nk=2^n$ in $\mathbb N$ ([[cor-binomial-theorem-consequences]] clause 1).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compare the two index sets of the occupation basis with the configuration sets, count them with the cited finite-counting facts, and read the vanishing statement off the antisymmetric sector.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Fermionic configurations] Let $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ have $|J|=n$; its indicator $\mathbf 1_J$ lies in $\{0,1\}^d$ with $\sum_j\mathbf 1_J(j)=n$. Conversely, if $\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d$ has $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$, then $J_\lambda:=\{j:\lambda_j=1\}$ satisfies $|J_\lambda|=n$ and $\mathbf 1_{J_\lambda}=\lambda$. The two assignments are inverse bijections, so the number of fermionic configurations of total occupation $n$ equals the number of $n$-element subsets, which is $\binom dn$ by [F2]; by [F1] this is $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$, which is the first assertion of (a). [F1, F2, algebra, construct]

1.2 [Bosonic configurations] The assignment $\lambda\mapsto m_\lambda$ is injective by the linear independence of the orthogonal family [F1], and its image spans $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, so it is a bijection onto the set of basis lines; the number of its elements is $|W(n,d)|=\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$ by [F3] and [F2], the first assertion of (b). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Fermionic row sum] Summing the dimensions over all particle numbers and using [F1] for $n\le d$ and the vanishing for $n>d$ gives $\sum_{n=0}^d\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\sum_{n=0}^d\binom dn=2^d$ by the row sum [F5], which completes (a). [F1, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Truncated bosonic dimension] For every $n$ the dimension $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}=\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}$ is given by step 1.2 and [F2]; hence $\sum_{n=0}^{N}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}$. Substituting $i:=n+d-1$, the terms with $i<d-1$ vanish by the boundary values of the binomial coefficient, so the hockey stick [F4] with $k=d-1$ and upper index $N+d-1$ gives $\sum_{i=0}^{N+d-1}\binom{i}{d-1}=\binom{N+d}{d}$; this completes (b). [F2, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 [Exclusion counts] By construction every fermionic configuration lies in $\{0,1\}^d$, so no entry is $\ge2$; for $n>d$ the set $\{0,1\}^d\cap\{\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ is empty because at most $d$ entries can be equal to $1$, and then $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ by [F1], while for the bosonic sector the configuration $\lambda^{(j)}$ with $\lambda^{(j)}_j=n$ and all other entries $0$ lies in $W(n,d)$ for every $j$, so no occupation bound holds there; this is (c). [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Consistency and assembly] Each $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ satisfies $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$ by definition, and each fermionic configuration in $\{0,1\}^d\cap\{\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ does so as well, which is (d); step 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), steps 1.2 and 2.2 prove (b), and step 2.3 proves (c). Only the cited spectral basis and finite-counting facts were used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Reading.** The theorem is the finite-mode bookkeeping behind the
  occupation-number description: for a $d$-mode one-particle space there are
  $\binom dn$ antisymmetric $n$-particle sector dimensions and
  $\binom{n+d-1}{n}$ symmetric ones, and the antisymmetric configurations have
  all occupations in $\{0,1\}$ while the symmetric ones do not. The physical
  reading of the occupations as a readout of the framework is fixed on
  [[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] and
  [[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]].
- **Truncation.** The sums over $n\le N$ are finite sums of finite
  dimensions; no infinite Fock space and no convergence statement is made
  here.

items.title: Regrouping two factors: the symmetry decomposition of a two-particle sector over an orbital and an internal factor
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,V$ be
nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]),
$\dim H=m$, $\dim V=k$. All tensor products below are the completed tensor
products of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with
elementary tensors $u\otimes v$, and all permutation projections
$P_\pm^{(2)}$ and exchange operators $\tau_W$ are those of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] and
[[lem-nrqm-identical-particles-two-particle-exchange-operator]] for the
displayed Hilbert space $W$. Then:

(a) *identification*: the inclusion $\kappa:H\odot V\to H\widehat\otimes V$ of the algebraic tensor product is a surjective linear isometry, so elementary tensors and finite sums of them may be treated as elements of the completed product without ambiguity; the same holds for $(H\otimes V)\widehat\otimes(H\otimes V)$ and $(H\otimes H)\widehat\otimes(V\otimes V)$;

(b) *regrouping unitary*: there is a unique bounded linear operator $\Theta:(H\otimes V)\widehat\otimes(H\otimes V)\to(H\otimes H)\widehat\otimes(V\otimes V)$ with
$$\Theta\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)=(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')$$
for all $u,v\in H$, $\chi,\chi'\in V$; $\Theta$ is unitary and its inverse is the unique bounded operator with $\Theta^{-1}\bigl((u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')\bigr)=(u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')$;

(c) *exchange intertwining*: $\Theta\,\tau_{H\otimes V}=(\tau_H\otimes\tau_V)\,\Theta$, where $\tau_H\otimes\tau_V$ is the bounded tensor product of the two exchange operators;

(d) *symmetriser identities*: $\Theta P_-^{(H\otimes V)}=\bigl(P_-^{(H)}\otimes P_+^{(V)}+P_+^{(H)}\otimes P_-^{(V)}\bigr)\Theta$ and $\Theta P_+^{(H\otimes V)}=\bigl(P_+^{(H)}\otimes P_+^{(V)}+P_-^{(H)}\otimes P_-^{(V)}\bigr)\Theta$; consequently $\Theta$ maps $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H\otimes V)}$ onto the orthogonal direct sum $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$ and $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(H\otimes V)}$ onto $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$;

(e) *vector identities*: for all $u,v\in H$ and $\chi,\chi'\in V$,
$$\Theta\Bigl(P_-^{(H\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)\Bigr)=P_+^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi')+P_-^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi'),$$
$$\Theta\Bigl(P_+^{(H\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)\Bigr)=P_+^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi')+P_-^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi');$$

(f) *dimensions*:
$$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H\otimes V)}=\binom m2\binom{k+1}2+\binom{m+1}2\binom k2=\binom{mk}2,$$
with the two summands of (d) having dimensions $\binom m2\binom{k+1}2$ and $\binom{m+1}2\binom k2$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite-dimensional nonzero complex Hilbert spaces $H,V$ of dimensions $m,k$, their completed tensor products, the elementary tensors and the permutation projections and exchange operators of the cited items.

[F1] **Tensor construction.** For complex Hilbert spaces $X,Y$ the inclusion $\kappa:X\odot Y\to X\widehat\otimes Y$ is a linear isometry with dense image; $\kappa(u\otimes v)$ is bilinear, $\|\kappa(u\otimes v)\|=\|u\|\,\|v\|$ and $\langle\kappa(u\otimes v),\kappa(u'\otimes v')\rangle=\langle u,u'\rangle\langle v,v'\rangle$; every element of $X\odot Y$ is a finite sum of elementary tensors, and if $(e_a)$ and $(f_b)$ are orthonormal bases of $X$ and $Y$ then $(\kappa(e_a\otimes f_b))$ is an orthonormal basis of $X\widehat\otimes Y$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F2] **Multilinear factorisation.** For a finite list of modules $M_1,\dots,M_k$ over a commutative ring, every parenthesised tensor product represents multilinear maps from $M_1\times\cdots\times M_k$, and different parenthesizations are connected by the unique isomorphism preserving pure tensors ([[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]).

[F3] **Finite-dimensional subspaces are closed.** A subspace of a normed space that admits a finite basis is closed ([[cor-finite-dimensional-subspaces-are-closed]]).

[F4] **Exchange operators and projections.** For a Hilbert space $W$, the exchange operator $\tau_W:=U_{(12)}$ satisfies $\tau_W^2=I$ and $\tau_W^{*}=\tau_W$ and $\tau_W(w\otimes w')=w'\otimes w$, and $P_\pm^{(W)}=\frac12(I\pm\tau_W)$ are the orthogonal projections with the corresponding ranges ([[lem-nrqm-identical-particles-two-particle-exchange-operator]] clauses (a),(b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (a),(c)).

[F5] **Bounded tensor maps.** For bounded operators $S,S'$ on $X$ and $T,T'$ on $Y$ there is a unique bounded $S\otimes T$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$, $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\|T\|$, $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$, $(S\otimes T)^{*}=S^{*}\otimes T^{*}$, and unitarity of $S,T$ gives unitarity of $S\otimes T$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (a)-(d), [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]).

[F6] **Dimensions.** For finite-dimensional vector spaces $X,Y$ over a field one has $\dim(X\otimes Y)=\dim X\cdot\dim Y$ ([[cor-tensor-products-of-finite-free-modules-and-dimension]]); and $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$, $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}n$ for a $d$-dimensional space ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F7] **Orthogonal projections.** If $P,Q$ are orthogonal projections with $PQ=QP=0$, then $P+Q$ is an orthogonal projection with $\operatorname{ran}(P+Q)=\operatorname{ran}P+\operatorname{ran}Q$ a direct sum of orthogonal subspaces; a product $P\otimes Q$ of orthogonal projections is an orthogonal projection ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the finite-dimensional algebraic and completed tensor products, build the regrouping map from the multilinear factorisation of the four-variable assignment, verify inversion and isometry on elementary tensors, transfer the exchange and symmetriser identities from elementary tensors by linearity, and read the decompositions and dimensions off the resulting projection identities.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [Identification] By [F1] the inclusion $\kappa:H\odot V\to H\widehat\otimes V$ is a linear isometry with dense image; if $(e_1,\dots,e_m)$ and $(f_1,\dots,f_k)$ are orthonormal bases of $H$ and $V$, then the $mk$ elements $e_a\otimes f_b$ span the algebraic tensor product by bilinearity, so $\kappa[H\odot V]$ is a finite-dimensional subspace of the Hilbert space $H\widehat\otimes V$, hence closed by [F3], and a dense closed subspace is the whole space; thus $\kappa$ is onto and identifies the two spaces, and the same argument applies to the algebraic and completed tensor products of $H\otimes V$ with itself and of $H\otimes H$ with $V\otimes V$, whose algebraic parts are spanned by finitely many elementary tensors. This proves (a). [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 [The regrouping map and its inverse] Define $\Phi(u,v,\chi,\chi'):=(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')$ for $u,v\in H$, $\chi,\chi'\in V$; it is multilinear in its four arguments, so by [F2] it corresponds to a unique linear map on the four-fold algebraic tensor product and, by the parenthesization independence of [F2] together with the identification of step 1.1, to a unique linear map $\Theta$ on $(H\otimes V)\widehat\otimes(H\otimes V)$ with the displayed values on elementary tensors; uniqueness holds because those elementary tensors span the space. Likewise $\Psi\bigl((u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')\bigr):=(u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')$ is multilinear and defines a linear map $\Psi$ on $(H\otimes H)\widehat\otimes(V\otimes V)$. On elementary tensors $\Psi\Theta=\mathrm{id}$ and $\Theta\Psi=\mathrm{id}$, and two linear maps agreeing on a spanning set agree everywhere; hence $\Theta$ is a linear isomorphism with inverse $\Psi$, which is the existence and inverse statement of (b). [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

3.1 [Unitarity] For elementary tensors $x=(u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')$ and $y=(u'\otimes\chi'')\otimes(v'\otimes\chi''')$ in the domain the inner-product identities of [F1] give $\langle\Theta x,\Theta y\rangle=\langle u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'\rangle\langle\chi\otimes\chi',\chi''\otimes\chi'''\rangle=\langle u,u'\rangle\langle v,v'\rangle\langle\chi,\chi''\rangle\langle\chi',\chi'''\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle$; the difference of the two sesquilinear forms vanishes on all pairs of elementary tensors, and since every vector is a finite sum of elementary tensors by [F1] it vanishes identically, so $\Theta$ is an isometry; being invertible by step 2.1 it is unitary, which completes (b). [F1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 [Intertwining with the exchange operators] For $u,v\in H$, $\chi,\chi'\in V$ one computes with [F4] and [F5] that $\Theta\tau_{H\otimes V}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)=\Theta\bigl((v\otimes\chi')\otimes(u\otimes\chi)\bigr)=(v\otimes u)\otimes(\chi'\otimes\chi)$ and $(\tau_H\otimes\tau_V)\Theta\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)=(\tau_H\otimes\tau_V)\bigl((u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')\bigr)=(v\otimes u)\otimes(\chi'\otimes\chi)$; both sides are bounded linear maps agreeing on the spanning set of elementary tensors, so they agree everywhere, which is (c). [F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Symmetriser identities] By [F4], $P_\pm^{(H\otimes V)}=\frac12(I\pm\tau_{H\otimes V})$, $P_\pm^{(H)}=\frac12(I\pm\tau_H)$ and $P_\pm^{(V)}=\frac12(I\pm\tau_V)$; using step 3.2 to move $\Theta$ past $\tau_{H\otimes V}$ and the linearity and multiplicativity of the tensor product of operators [F5], one obtains on the whole space $\Theta P_-^{(H\otimes V)}=\frac12\Theta-\frac12(\tau_H\otimes\tau_V)\Theta=\bigl(\frac12-\frac12\tau_H\otimes\tau_V\bigr)\Theta=\bigl(P_-^{(H)}\otimes P_+^{(V)}+P_+^{(H)}\otimes P_-^{(V)}\bigr)\Theta$, because $\frac12(I-\tau_H\otimes\tau_V)=\frac12(I-\tau_H)\otimes\frac12(I+\tau_V)+\frac12(I+\tau_H)\otimes\frac12(I-\tau_V)$ and its sign-reversed analogue are identities of bounded operators; this proves the first assertion of (d), and the computation with both signs reversed gives the second. [F4, F5, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 [Direct-sum decompositions] By [F7] the operators $P_-^{(H)}\otimes P_+^{(V)}$ and $P_+^{(H)}\otimes P_-^{(V)}$ are orthogonal projections whose product is $(P_-^{(H)}P_+^{(H)})\otimes(P_+^{(V)}P_-^{(V)})=0$, so their sum is an orthogonal projection with range the orthogonal direct sum of the two ranges; by step 4.1 and the unitarity of step 3.1, the image of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H\otimes V)}$ under $\Theta$ is that direct sum, and the same argument with the second identity of step 4.1 gives the symmetric-sector decomposition, completing (d). [F7, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 [Vector identities] Applying the first identity of step 4.1 to the elementary tensor $(u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')$ and using the linearity of $\Theta$ and of tensor products of operators gives $\Theta P_-^{(H\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)=\bigl(P_-^{(H)}\otimes P_+^{(V)}+P_+^{(H)}\otimes P_-^{(V)}\bigr)\bigl((u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')\bigr)=P_+^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi')+P_-^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi')$, which is the first identity of (e); the second follows in the same way from the second identity of step 4.1. [step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 [Dimensions] By step 5.1 and the unitarity of step 3.1, $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H\otimes V)}=\dim(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)})+\dim(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)})$; by [F6] applied to the $m$- and $k$-dimensional spaces this is $\binom m2\binom{k+1}2+\binom{m+1}2\binom k2$, which are the displayed summand dimensions, and expanding the two products gives $\frac{m(m-1)k(k+1)+m(m+1)k(k-1)}4=\frac{mk(mk-1)}2=\binom{mk}2$, which is (f). [F6, step 3.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 [Assembly] Step 1.1 proves (a), steps 2.1 and 3.1 prove (b), step 3.2 proves (c), steps 4.1 and 5.1 prove (d), step 5.2 proves (e) and step 6.1 proves (f). Only the cited linear algebra, tensor products and permutation projections were used, under the Countable Choice hypotheses of [F1], [F2] and [F5]; no physical reading of the factors is asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 5.2, step 6.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Reading of the decomposition.** With $H$ an orbital factor and $V$ an internal (spin) factor, the first summand of the antisymmetric sector pairs antisymmetric orbital two-vectors with symmetric internal two-vectors and the second pairs symmetric orbital two-vectors with antisymmetric internal two-vectors, so the internal permutation symmetry is opposite to the orbital one. The physical use of this identity for two spin-half fermions is on the examples page ([[texp-nrqm-identical-particles-two-fermion-spatial-spin-symmetry]]).
- **Finite dimension.** Both factors are finite dimensional, so the algebraic and completed tensor products are identified in (a); no infinite-dimensional regrouping is asserted, and the identities themselves are transferred from elementary tensors by linearity.

items.title: Declared species sectors and their preparations: the framework's reading of P6
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\,\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; a bounded quantity
preserves the sector exactly when it commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the
framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

## Remarks

- **Labels versus particles.** The tensor factors of $H^{\otimes n}$ are
  bookkeeping slots, not particle identities: by clause (c) the model assigns
  the same sector state to every relabelling, and clause (f) of P6 records
  that the labels carry no physical content.
- **Why the sector restriction is stated for operators.** The rule of clause
  (e) is the one recorded in the owner direction for permutation sectors: a
  bounded quantity restricts to a sector only when it preserves the sector.
  Position and momentum operators of a single labelled factor do not preserve
  either sector, which is why they are not read as sector quantities.

The sector assignment is an adopted model assumption of P6; the definition derives nothing about nature, asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no dynamics, no measurement law beyond P2 and no empirical fact.

items.title: The declared finite-mode model and its occupation readouts
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt a declared species sector in the vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
the observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) The declared finite-mode model.** Fix $d\ge1$, a finite-dimensional
complex Hilbert space $K$ of dimension $d$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with a
declared orthonormal basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, the **declared modes** of the
model, and an integer $n\ge1$. The **declared finite-mode model** of the
species with these data is the declared species sector of clause (a) whose
one-particle space is $K$, together with its $n$-particle sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq K^{\otimes n}$
and the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
clauses (c)-(d). The declaration is an idealization: it asserts that the model
confines the one-particle content to the $d$ declared modes. No claim is made
that a species has finitely many modes; whether the declared modes describe a
laboratory mode family is a tested identification with uncertainty under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a consequence of this definition.

**(c) The occupation readouts.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ let
$$N_j:K^{\otimes n}\to K^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n}\rangle\,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\},$$
be the occupation operator of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (d) for the
basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$. By that clause $N_j$ is bounded and self-adjoint, the
$N_j$ commute pairwise, and $N_j$ preserves the sector $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$;
the **sector occupation readout** is the restriction
$$N_j^\sigma:=N_j|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},$$
a bounded self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ with spectrum
contained in $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. The model reads $(N_j^\sigma,\text{particle
count})$ as an assigned sharp observable of the declared sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a):
its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\, E_{N_j^\sigma}(B)\bigr),\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
the reading of P2 clause (ii) through the observable definition.

**(d) The joint occupation readout.** The operators $N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma$
are simultaneously diagonalised by the sector bases of the cited theorem: the
Slater basis in the fermionic case and the family $(m_\lambda)$ in the
bosonic case, with joint eigenvalues $\mathbf 1_J$ and $\lambda$ respectively.
Write $\Lambda_n:=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\lambda_j\le n,\
\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ and, for $\lambda\in\Lambda_n$, let $P_\lambda$ be the
orthogonal projection of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ onto the joint eigenspace of
$(N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma)$ for the eigenvalue vector $\lambda$; the cited
theorem exhibits these eigenspaces as the lines spanned by the corresponding
sector basis vectors, so the $P_\lambda$ are mutually orthogonal, their finite
sum is the identity of the sector, and $N_j^\sigma=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
\lambda_jP_\lambda$. The model reads the **joint occupation readout** through
the finite family $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}$: the joint law in a
declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)\qquad (\lambda\in\Lambda_n),$$
and the marginal law of $N_j^\sigma$ is recovered by
$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\sum_{\lambda:\lambda_j\in B}\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)$,
because the eigenvalue decomposition of $N_j^\sigma$ groups the $P_\lambda$
by the value $\lambda_j$.

**(e) Total occupation.** By clause (d) of the cited theorem,
$\sum_{j=1}^{d}N_j^\sigma=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$; hence the
**total occupation** $\sum_jN_j^\sigma$ has the degenerate outcome law
$\delta_n$ in every declared sector preparation, and the joint law is
supported on $\Lambda_n$: the total number of particles read by the model is
$n$ with certainty.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of the model and
read the cited spectral mathematics through P2; they add no assumption beyond
the sector declaration and the finite-mode idealization of clause (b). The
occupation readouts are sector quantities in the sense of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]];
the exclusion and occupation-count consequences are proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]] and
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]]). No measured
count, no detector response, no dynamics and no empirical claim is made.

## Remarks

- **Mode versus particle.** $N_j^\sigma$ counts how many of the $n$ particles
  the model reads in the declared mode $f_j$; it is a collective readout of
  the sector, not a quantity of a labelled factor, and it is insensitive to
  which labels carry the occupied modes.
- **Choice hypotheses.** The tensor construction and the sector projections
  carry the Axiom of Countable Choice, which is declared in clause (a); the
  finite spectral decomposition of clause (d) is finite-dimensional and uses
  no further choice.

The finite mode family is a declared idealization of the model, its identification with any laboratory mode set is a tested physical identification with uncertainty, and the definition asserts no measured count, no dynamics and no empirical result.

items.title: Permutation invariance of sector preparations and the indistinguishability of relabelled readouts
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral mathematics. Let a species sector with parameters
$(H,m,s,\sigma)$, integer $n\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}$ and permutation
unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$ be declared, and let $\rho$ be a declared
sector preparation. Then:

(a) *invariance of the preparation*: $U_\pi\rho U_\pi^{*}=\rho$ for every
$\pi\in S_n$;

(b) *indistinguishability of relabelled readouts*: for every $\pi$ and every
assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ of the labelled model (a densely defined
self-adjoint operator on $H^{\otimes n}$ with a declared unit), the operator
$A_\pi:=U_\pi AU_\pi^{*}$ with domain $U_\pi D(A)$ is an assigned sharp
observable of the labelled model with the same unit, and for every Borel set
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$
$$\mu^{A_\pi}_\rho(B)=\mu^{A}_\rho(B);$$
for bounded $A$ this reads
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,U_\pi AU_\pi^{*})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$;

(c) *sector-preserving quantities*: if $A$ is an assigned sharp observable
that preserves the sector and satisfies $U_\pi AU_\pi^{*}=A$ on its domain for
every $\pi$, then $A$ induces the sector quantity of clause (e) of the sector
definition and its law on sector preparations is the same as that of
$A_\pi=A$.

The theorem is conditional on the adopted sector: it establishes that within
the model no assigned readout of the labelled space can distinguish the labels,
and it asserts nothing about which statistics a physical species realizes.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A declared species sector $(H,m,s,\sigma)$, $n\ge1$, the sector space and permutation unitaries, a declared sector preparation $\rho$, and an assigned sharp observable $A$.

[F1] **Sector vocabulary.** $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}$ is a closed subspace of $H^{\otimes n}$, every $U_\pi$ is unitary and preserves $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$, acting there as the scalar $\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)$ with $\operatorname{sgn}_+=1$ and $\operatorname{sgn}_-=\operatorname{sgn}$; a declared sector preparation is a density operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$, read as a state of the framework ([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]] clauses (c)-(d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (a),(c)).

[F2] **Observable reading.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, and the outcome law in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

[F3] **Unitary transport of spectral measures.** If $U$ is a bijective linear isometry of a Hilbert space and $T$ a self-adjoint operator, then $T':=UTU^{-1}$ with domain $UD(T)$ is self-adjoint and its spectral projection-valued measure is $E_{T'}(B)=UE_T(B)U^{-1}$ ([[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a),(b), [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F4] **Cyclicity of the trace.** If $T$ is trace class and $S$ bounded, then $ST$ and $TS$ are trace class with $\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\operatorname{tr}(TS)$ ([[thm-cyclicity-of-the-trace]]).

[F5] **States.** A state on a Hilbert space is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator of trace one; pure states are the rank-one operators of unit rays ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; use the scalar action of the permutation unitaries on the sector to prove the invariance of the preparation, transport it through the spectral measure of a relabelled observable by the unitary transport lemma, and compare the outcome laws with the cyclic property of the trace.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Invariance] Let $x,y\in\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$. By [F1] one has $U_\pi^{*}x=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)^{-1}x=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)x$ and likewise for $y$, so $\langle U_\pi\rho U_\pi^{*}x,y\rangle=\langle\rho U_\pi^{*}x,U_\pi^{*}y\rangle=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)^{2}\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle\rho x,y\rangle$ by the unitarity of $U_\pi$ and the sesquilinearity of the inner product. Since $x,y$ are arbitrary, $U_\pi\rho U_\pi^{*}=\rho$; multiplying this identity on the left by $U_\pi^{*}$ and on the right by $U_\pi$ and using $U_\pi^{*}U_\pi=I$ gives $U_\pi^{*}\rho U_\pi=\rho$ as well. This proves (a). [F1, F5, algebra]

1.2 [Sector-preserving case] If $A$ preserves the sector and $U_\pi AU_\pi^{*}=A$ on its domain for every $\pi$, then $A_\pi=A$ and clause (b) is vacuous for such $A$; the sector restriction of clause (e) of the sector definition is the quantity read on sector preparations, and its law agrees with the law of $A$ by [F2]. This is (c). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Relabelled laws] Fix $\pi$ and an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$. Since $U_\pi$ is a bijective linear isometry of $H^{\otimes n}$ and $A$ is self-adjoint, [F3] gives that $A_\pi=U_\pi AU_\pi^{*}$ is self-adjoint on the domain $U_\pi D(A)$ with spectral measure $E_{A_\pi}(B)=U_\pi E_A(B)U_\pi^{*}$. Hence for every preparation $\rho$ and Borel $B$, $\mu^{A_\pi}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho U_\pi E_A(B)U_\pi^{*})$ by [F2]. Because $\rho$ is trace class and $U_\pi E_A(B)$ is bounded, [F4] applied twice gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho U_\pi E_A(B)U_\pi^{*})=\operatorname{tr}(U_\pi^{*}\rho U_\pi E_A(B))$; by step 1.1 the middle factor is $\rho$, so $\mu^{A_\pi}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\mu^{A}_\rho(B)$, which is (b) in the general form; for bounded $A$ the same computation with $A$ in place of $E_A(B)$ gives the displayed trace identity. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), step 2.1 proves (b) and step 1.2 proves (c). The proof uses only the adopted sector of P6, the readings of P1 and P2, and the cited spectral and trace mathematics under the declared choice hypotheses; no measured invariance, no dynamics and no species assignment is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the theorem does and does not say.** The invariance is a property of
  every state the model declares on a sector, and it is what makes the tensor
  labels unobservable inside the model; it does not say that the labels are
  meaningless in intermediate manipulations, and it does not by itself force a
  permutation-invariant preparation into a sector, which is a separate
  question not treated here.
- **Relation to the occupation readout.** Every occupation readout of the
  declared finite-mode model is a sector quantity built from the operators
  $N_j$, which commute with all $U_\pi$ because they are diagonal in the
  product basis and count index occurrences
  ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (d)); the
  exclusion consequences for those readouts are the subject of the next
  theorem of this page.

The result is conditional on the adopted sector of P6 and on P1-P2; it asserts no measured invariance, no dynamics and no spin-statistics theorem.

items.title: Pauli exclusion in the declared finite-mode occupation readout, with the bosonic contrast
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]], and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Declare a finite-mode
model as in
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] with $d$
declared modes $f_1,\dots,f_d$, $n\ge1$ particles and statistics choice
$\sigma$, with sector space $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$,
occupation readouts $N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma$, joint projections
$(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}$ and joint law
$\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)$. Then for every
declared sector preparation $\rho$:

(a) *fermionic exclusion*: if $\sigma=-$, then
$$\mu^{N_j^-}_\rho\bigl([2,\infty)\bigr)=0\quad(j=1,\dots,d), \qquad \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,N_j^-(N_j^--I)\bigr)=0,$$
and the joint law is supported on the occupation configurations with entries in
$\{0,1\}$:
$$\mu^{N}_\rho\bigl(\{\lambda\in\Lambda_n:\lambda_j\ge2\ \text{for some }j\}\bigr)=0;$$

(b) *no restriction in the symmetric sector*: if $\sigma=+$, then for every
$\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the projection $P_\lambda$ is nonzero, and for the pure
declared sector preparation of the ray of $m_\lambda$ the joint law gives
weight one to $\lambda$; in particular for $n\ge2$ and any $j$ the
configuration with $\lambda_j=n$ occurs;

(c) *total occupation*: in either sector $\sum_{j=1}^{d}N_j^\sigma
=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$, so the total occupation has the
degenerate law $\delta_n$ and every outcome of the joint readout satisfies
$\sum_j\lambda_j=n$.

The exclusion in (a) is a conditional consequence of the adopted antisymmetric
sector and of the declared finite-mode readout; the theorem asserts no measured
occupancy, no detector behaviour and no derivation of the statistics of any
species.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A declared finite-mode model with $d$ modes, $n\ge1$ particles, statistics choice $\sigma$, sector space, occupation readouts, joint projections and a declared sector preparation $\rho$.

[F1] **Sector readouts.** $K$ is $d$-dimensional with orthonormal basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$; the operators $N_j$ of the occupation theorem are bounded self-adjoint, commute pairwise, satisfy $\sum_jN_j=nI$ and preserve both sector spaces, with $N_jf_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)f_J^\wedge$ and $N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_jm_\lambda$, and the joint eigenspaces inside $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$ are the lines $\mathbb Cf_J^\wedge$ (indexed by $n$-element subsets $J$, eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$) and inside $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ (indexed by $\lambda\in W(n,d)$, eigenvalue vector $\lambda$) ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (b)-(d), [[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] clauses (c)-(d)).

[F2] **Observable reading.** An assigned sharp observable $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and the outcome law $\mu^{A}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$; if a projection-valued measure $F$ satisfies $\int\lambda\,dF(\lambda)=A$, then $F=E_A$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

[F3] **Finite spectral decomposition.** If a finite-dimensional Hilbert space has an orthogonal basis of eigenvectors of a self-adjoint operator $A$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_k$ and the $Q_k$ are the orthogonal projections onto the eigenspaces, then $B\mapsto\sum_{\lambda_k\in B}Q_k$ is a projection-valued measure on the Borel sets with $\int\lambda\,dF(\lambda)=A$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

[F4] **Laws and traces.** For a preparation $\rho$ and projections $P_\lambda$ with $\sum_\lambda P_\lambda=I$ the numbers $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)$ are nonnegative and sum to one; a pure preparation of the unit ray of a vector $x\ne0$ gives weight $\|Qx\|^2/\|x\|^2$ to an orthogonal projection $Q$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clauses (a),(b), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

[F5] **Configuration counts.** No fermionic configuration has an entry $\ge2$; for $n>d$ the antisymmetric sector is $\{0\}$; every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ is a bosonic configuration, including the configuration with $\lambda_j=n$ for any $j$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),(c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; diagonalise the sector restrictions of the occupation operators in the sector bases, identify their finite spectral measures, and read the support of the joint law off the eigenvalue vectors.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Sector restrictions are self-adjoint] By [F1] the operator $N_j$ preserves $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$, and both the Slater family and the family $(m_\lambda)$ consist of eigenvectors of $N_j$ with real eigenvalues and form a basis of the respective sector; a linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space that is diagonal in an orthogonal basis with real eigenvalues is self-adjoint. Hence each $N_j^\sigma=N_j|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$ is a bounded self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$, which is the readout declared in clauses (c)-(d) of the model. [F1, algebra]

2.1 [Finite spectral measures and laws] Let $\sigma=-$ and index the Slater basis as $f_J^\wedge$ with $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$, $|J|=n$; by [F1] each $f_J^\wedge$ is a joint eigenvector of $(N_1^-,\dots,N_d^-)$ with eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$, and the eigenspaces are the lines $\mathbb Cf_J^\wedge$. For fixed $j$ the eigenspaces of $N_j^-$ are obtained by grouping the lines by the value $\mathbf 1_J(j)\in\{0,1\}$; the orthogonal projection onto the range of $N_j^-$ is therefore $Q_1:=\sum_{J:j\in J}P_{\mathbf 1_J}$ and the orthogonal projection onto the kernel is $Q_0:=I-Q_1$, and $N_j^-=Q_1$ because $N_j^-$ acts as $1$ on $\operatorname{ran}Q_1$ and $0$ on $\operatorname{ran}Q_0$. By [F2] and [F3] the spectral measure of $N_j^-$ is $E_{N_j^-}(B)=\sum_{\lambda\in B\cap\{0,1\}}Q_\lambda$, so for a Borel set $B$ the outcome law is $\mu^{N_j^-}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{N_j^-}(B))$; the same argument in the symmetric sector replaces $\mathbf 1_J$ by $\lambda$ and gives the spectral measures of $N_j^+$. This identifies the readout laws of clauses (c)-(d) of the model. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

3.1 [Exclusion] Assume $\sigma=-$. By step 2.1 the spectral measure of $N_j^-$ is supported on $\{0,1\}$, so $E_{N_j^-}([2,\infty))=0$ and $\mu^{N_j^-}_\rho([2,\infty))=\operatorname{tr}(0)=0$; moreover $N_j^-(N_j^--I)=0$ on the sector because the operator vanishes on the Slater basis by [F1], so its expectation $\operatorname{tr}(\rho N_j^-(N_j^--I))$ is zero. For the joint law, [F1] shows that the joint eigenspaces with an entry $\ge2$ do not occur among the lines $\mathbb Cf_J^\wedge$, so the sum of the corresponding projections $P_\lambda$ is zero and $\mu^{N}_\rho(\{\lambda:\lambda_j\ge2\ \text{for some }j\})=0$. This proves (a). [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 [Bosonic contrast] Assume $\sigma=+$. For every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the vector $m_\lambda$ is nonzero and spans the joint eigenspace for $\lambda$ by [F1], so $P_\lambda\ne0$; for the pure preparation of the ray of $m_\lambda$ the weight is $\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)=\|P_\lambda x\|^2/\|x\|^2=1$ for any unit representative $x$ of that ray by [F4]. By [F5] the configurations $\lambda$ with $\lambda_j=n$ lie in $W(n,d)$, so they occur; this proves (b). [F1, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

3.3 [Total occupation] By [F1] one has $\sum_jN_j=nI$ on the whole tensor power, hence on the sector, and therefore $\sum_jN_j^\sigma=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$; since the total occupation is the constant operator $nI$, its outcome law assigns probability one to $\{n\}$ in every preparation, and applying the joint law of [F1] gives $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$ for every configuration of the support; this is (c). [F1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 3.1 proves (a), step 3.2 proves (b) and step 3.3 proves (c). The proof is conditional on the declared sector of P6, the declared finite-mode readout and the cited spectral mathematics; no measured occupancy, no apparatus behaviour and no derivation of a species' statistics is asserted. [step 3.1, step 3.2, step 3.3] ∎

## Remarks

- **The precise content of "exclusion".** The theorem states the vanishing of
  the probability of reading an occupation $\ge2$ in each declared mode and
  the vanishing of the expectation of the double-occupation operator
  $N_j(N_j-1)$; it is a statement about the declared readout in every declared
  sector preparation, not a statement about particles avoiding each other in
  space.
- **Finite modes.** The statement uses the finite-dimensional mode model of
  the definition; the counting facts for the index sets are those of the
  finite-mode count theorem. No infinite mode family and no continuum
  occupancy is treated.

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Chapter 1 Sections 1.2-1.3 pp. 5-9: occupation-number states with fermionic occupations in {0,1} and no such restriction for bosons

The statement is conditional on the declared sector and the finite-mode idealization; it asserts no measured occupancy, no apparatus claim and no derivation of a species' statistics.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the identical-particles page
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**Adopted assumptions.** The page adopts the sector and species assignments of
P6 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]:
which species is bosonic or fermionic, its mass, charge, spin label and
statistics are declared model parameters, and the symmetric or antisymmetric
sector of the $n$-particle space is part of that declaration. The finite-mode
occupation model of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] adds the
declared finite mode family as an idealization. These are assumptions of the
model, not consequences of the Hilbert-space formalism and not measurements.

**Conditional results.** The mathematical items of the page construct the two
permutation sectors and their occupation bases
([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]]), count the
occupation configurations ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]])
and decompose a two-factor sector into opposite-symmetry summands
([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]]). The
physical results are conditional on the adopted sector:
[[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]] proves that sector
preparations and relabelled readouts are statistically indistinguishable, and
[[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]] proves the
exclusion of double occupations in the antisymmetric sector together with the
bosonic contrast. All of these are deductions from the stated postulates,
idealizations and mathematical hypotheses.

**What is not claimed.** The page does not derive the spin-statistics
connection: the relativistic theorem is outside this framework and the link
between the spin label and the sector is a declared model assignment
(clause (iv) of P6). It does not claim that the declared modes are an exact
description of any apparatus or species, does not treat infinite mode families
or the continuum of modes, and introduces no dynamics of the sector, no
interaction and no instrument; the interaction example of the companion page
is a conditional computation in a declared model. Nothing on the page
attributes particle-like trajectories, spatial avoidance or a force to the
exclusion statement.

**Empirical status.** The page records no measurement and no data. Whether some
laboratory ensemble realizes a declared sector preparation, a declared mode
family or a declared apparatus is a tested identification with uncertainty
under the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; comparisons of model
predictions with counts would test the combined model and apparatus
assumptions, and agreement would be evidence, not a deductive proof of the
model. The design's separate dedicated statistics treatment is a named
destination of the later many-body page and is not silently claimed here.

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Chapter 1 Sections 1.1-1.4 pp. 3-13: identical particles, the two sectors, and the scope of the occupation-number description
