items.title: The two spin-half fermion sector: the spin-singlet and spin-triplet parts and their orbital symmetry
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the
readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Declare a
**spin-half fermionic species** whose one-particle space is the completed
product $K\widehat\otimes V$ of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert
space $K$ (the orbital factor) with $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ (the internal factor of
P6 clause (ii) for $s=\tfrac12$), with $V$ carrying the orthonormal basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$ of [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]], and
declare $n=2$ particles in the adopted antisymmetric sector
$$\mathfrak H_2^-=\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\subseteq (K\otimes V)\widehat\otimes(K\otimes V)$$
of the declared species, with the regrouping unitary $\Theta$ of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]]. Write
$u\wedge v:=\sqrt2\,P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ and
$u\odot v:=\sqrt2\,P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ for $u,v\in K$, and
$\sigma_\pm:=(e_+\otimes e_-\pm e_-\otimes e_+)/\sqrt2$ for the spin
combinations. Then, as conditional statements of the declared model:

(a) *sector decomposition*: $\Theta$ carries $\mathfrak H_2^-$ onto the
orthogonal direct sum $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$,
where $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}=\mathbb C\Psi$ is the one-dimensional
spin-singlet line spanned by the singlet $\Psi$ of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] clause (d) and
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}=W_{1}$ is the three-dimensional spin-triplet
space of that theorem; consequently the antisymmetric two-particle sector is
the sum of a **spin-singlet part** $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\mathbb C\Psi$,
of dimension $\binom{m+1}2$ for $m=\dim K$, with symmetric orbital factor,
and a **spin-triplet part** $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes W_1$, of
dimension $3\binom m2$, with antisymmetric orbital factor;

(b) *opposite orbital symmetry*: for all $u,v\in K$ and $\chi,\chi'\in V$,
$$\Theta\Bigl(P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)\Bigr) =P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi') +P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi');$$
the spin-singlet component therefore multiplies the symmetric orbital
component and the spin-triplet component multiplies the antisymmetric orbital
component, so within each component the orbital exchange symmetry is opposite
to the spin exchange symmetry;

(c) *parallel spins*: if $u,v\in K$ are orthonormal and $\chi\in V$ is a unit
vector, then $\Theta$ carries the ray of
$P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi)\bigr)$ to the ray
of $P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$, whose unit representative
is $(u\wedge v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$; for $\chi=e_+$ this is the
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_z=\hbar$ triplet component with an antisymmetric orbital
factor;

(d) *antiparallel spins*: if $u,v\in K$ are orthonormal, then $\Theta$ carries
the ray of $P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes e_+)\otimes(v\otimes e_-)\bigr)$
to the ray of $\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl((u\odot v)\otimes\sigma_-
+(u\wedge v)\otimes\sigma_+\bigr)$, an equal-amplitude superposition of the
singlet component with symmetric orbital factor and the $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_z=0$
triplet component with antisymmetric orbital factor; in particular such an
antisymmetrised product of two orthonormal one-particle states has no definite
orbital exchange symmetry.

The model assignment of the antisymmetric sector is that of P6; the statements
above are conditional on it and assert no spin-statistics theorem, no
interaction, no dynamics and no measurement.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared spin-half fermionic species with orbital factor $K$ of dimension $m$, internal factor $V=\mathbb C^2$ with basis $(e_+,e_-)$, the two-particle antisymmetric sector, the regrouping unitary $\Theta$, and vectors $u,v\in K$, $\chi,\chi'\in V$.

[F1] **Sector vocabulary.** The sector space is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K\otimes V)}$ with the inner product of the completed tensor square, its vectors are the declared pure preparations of the two particles, and the exchange operator and projections act as in the cited lemmas ([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]] clauses (c)-(d), [[lem-nrqm-identical-particles-two-particle-exchange-operator]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F2] **Regrouping and its identities.** The regrouping unitary $\Theta$ is unitary with $\Theta\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)=(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')$, maps $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K\otimes V)}$ onto $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$, and satisfies the vector identity $\Theta P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)=P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi')+P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi')$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]] clauses (b),(d),(e)).

[F3] **Spin-half internal factor.** For $V=\mathbb C^2$ the total spin operators of [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] decompose $V\otimes V=W_0\oplus W_1$ with $\dim W_0=1$, $\dim W_1=3$; the vector $\Psi=(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+)/\sqrt2$ is a unit vector with $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_i\Psi=0$ for all $i$ and is, up to a phase, the unique element of the kernel of $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$; the products $e_m\otimes e_n$ are $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$-eigenvectors with weight $\hbar(m+n)$, so $e_+\otimes e_+$ has weight $\hbar$ and the combinations $\sigma_+=(e_+\otimes e_-+e_-\otimes e_+)/\sqrt2$ and $\sigma_-=(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+)/\sqrt2$ are unit vectors in $W_1$ and $W_0$ with $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$-weight $0$ ([[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] clauses (b),(c),(d)).

[F4] **Orbital symmetric and antisymmetric combinations.** For a Hilbert space $K$ and orthonormal $u,v\in K$ the vectors $u\odot v=\sqrt2P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ and $u\wedge v=\sqrt2P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ are orthonormal, and $P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ and $P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ are orthogonal eigenvectors of the exchange operator; moreover $P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi)=0$ for every $\chi\in V$ ([[lem-nrqm-identical-particles-two-particle-exchange-operator]] clauses (b),(c),(d)).

[F5] **Dimensions.** For a $d$-dimensional space, $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(2)}=\binom{d+1}2$ and $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(2)}=\binom d2$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (b),(c)); the dimensions of the two orthogonal summands add ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]] clause (f)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the two spin combinations of the internal factor with the antisymmetric and symmetric summands, transfer the regrouping vector identity to rays and read the compositions off the identity of the symmetry-decomposition theorem.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Decomposition of the internal factor] By [F3] the antisymmetric combination $\sigma_-$ spans $W_0$ and $\sigma_+,\ e_+\otimes e_+,\ e_-\otimes e_-$ span the three-dimensional space $W_1$; since $e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+$ is antisymmetric under the exchange and $e_+\otimes e_+,e_-\otimes e_-,e_+\otimes e_-+e_-\otimes e_+$ are symmetric, $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}=\mathbb C(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+)=\mathbb C\Psi=W_0$ and $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}=\operatorname{Sym}^2V=W_1$; the two subspaces are orthogonal complements of each other because $V\otimes V=W_0\oplus W_1$. [F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Sector decomposition] By [F2] the unitary image of the sector is $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$, an orthogonal direct sum, and step 1.1 identifies its summands as the spin-triplet part $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes W_1$ and the spin-singlet part $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes W_0$; by [F5] the singlet part has dimension $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}=\binom{m+1}2$, and the triplet part has dimension $3\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}=3\binom m2$; this is (a) up to the assignment of the names singlet and triplet, which is the naming of $W_0$ and $W_1$ in [F3]. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Opposite symmetry] The identity of (b) is the vector identity of [F2] under the identifications of steps 1.1 and 2.1: the first summand carries the internal factor in $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}=W_0$, the singlet, and the orbital factor in $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}$, the symmetric orbital component, while the second summand carries the internal factor in $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}=W_1$, the triplet, and the orbital factor in $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}$, the antisymmetric orbital component. This proves (b). [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Parallel spins] Let $u,v$ be orthonormal and $\chi$ a unit vector. By [F4] one has $P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi)=0$ and $P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi)=\chi\otimes\chi$; hence the identity of (b) gives $\Theta P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi)\bigr)=P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$, and multiplying by $\sqrt2$ gives the unit vector $(u\wedge v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$ because $\|u\wedge v\|=1$ and $\|\chi\otimes\chi\|=1$ by [F4]; both vectors lie in the sector and both rays are declared pure sector preparations by [F1], so the images of the two rays coincide, which is (c). [F1, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 [Antiparallel spins] Let $u,v$ be orthonormal. The orbital projections are $P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)=(u\odot v)/\sqrt2$ and $P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)=(u\wedge v)/\sqrt2$ by their definitions. In the internal tensor square, $P_-^{(V)}(e_+\otimes e_-)=\sigma_-/\sqrt2$ and $P_+^{(V)}(e_+\otimes e_-)=\sigma_+/\sqrt2$ by [F2] and the exchange formulas in [F4]. Substituting these four identities into (b) gives $\Theta P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes e_+)\otimes(v\otimes e_-)\bigr)=\tfrac12\bigl((u\odot v)\otimes\sigma_-+(u\wedge v)\otimes\sigma_+\bigr)$. The two tensor summands inside the parentheses are orthogonal unit vectors, by [F3] and [F4], so this complete projected vector has norm $1/\sqrt2$. Multiplying it by $\sqrt2$ gives the unit representative $\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl((u\odot v)\otimes\sigma_-+(u\wedge v)\otimes\sigma_+\bigr)$ of the image ray, as in (d). [F2, F3, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b), step 4.1 proves (c) and step 4.2 proves (d). Every statement is conditional on the adopted antisymmetric sector of P6 and on the declared finite orbital factor; the internal factor is the bookkeeping factor of P6 and no spatial position, interaction, dynamics or measurement is introduced. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **The singlet and triplet names.** The names refer to the total spin of the
  pair in the sense of the internal-factor composition theorem: $W_0$ is the
  kernel of $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ and $W_1$ is the triplet block. The orbital
  factor carries no spin and the theorem attributes no spin to the orbital
  degrees of freedom.
- **A Slater determinant is a superposition.** As clause (d) shows, the
  antisymmetrised product of two orthonormal one-particle states with opposite
  spin orientations contains both the singlet and the triplet $S_z=0$
  components with equal amplitudes; a definite orbital exchange symmetry
  belongs to the components, not to every vector of the sector.

D. Skinner, Principles of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge Part II, Michaelmas 2021), Chapter 7 'Identical Particles', pp. 4-10: exchange symmetry, spin, and the symmetric and antisymmetric decomposition of a two-particle state; Internet Archive copy of the original https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/dbs26/PQM/chap7.pdf

The computation is conditional on the adopted antisymmetric sector of P6 and on the declared finite orbital factor; it asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no interaction, no dynamics, no measurement and no empirical claim.

items.title: Exchange versus direct Coulomb terms: the pair-energy split of the two-orbital spin-half model
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the identical-particle and spin
postulate P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Declare the following
**two-orbital spin-half model**:

(a) the species is a spin-half fermion; its orbital factor is
$K:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{u,v\}$ where
$u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\cap L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
are real-valued, normalized and orthogonal in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), with $uv\ne0$ in $L^{1}$; the internal factor is $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ with basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$; the one-particle space is $K\widehat\otimes V$ and $n=2$
particles are declared in the antisymmetric sector
$\mathfrak H_2^-=\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K\otimes V)}$
([[texp-nrqm-identical-particles-two-fermion-spatial-spin-symmetry]]);

(b) write $E:=K\widehat\otimes K$ and let $J:E\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ be the restriction of the Euclidean product unitary $\Theta_6$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]), so $J(a\otimes b)(x,y)=a(x)b(y)$. The declared pair interaction is the compression of the Coulomb form to $E$: with $W(x-y)=\kappa/|x-y|$, $\kappa>0$, set
$$q(z,z'):=\int_{\mathbb R^6}W(x-y)(Jz)(x,y)\overline{(Jz')(x,y)}\,dx\,dy.$$
All $Jz$ lie in $D(M_W)$, as verified below. For the orthonormal basis $(b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4):=(u\otimes u,u\otimes v,v\otimes u,v\otimes v)$ of $E$, define
$$Az:=\sum_{j=1}^4q(z,b_j)b_j.$$
Thus $\langle Az,z'\rangle=q(z,z')$; $A$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator on $E$ with real matrix entries in this basis. It commutes with spatial exchange. The model's sector interaction is the restriction to $\mathfrak H_2^-$ of $\Theta^{-1}(A\otimes I_{V\otimes V})\Theta$, with $\Theta$ the finite-dimensional regrouping unitary of the symmetry-decomposition theorem. This restriction is well defined because the conjugated operator commutes with total exchange. On a factored preparation with unit $\chi$ its expectation is $q(\varphi,\varphi)=\langle M_WJ\varphi,J\varphi\rangle$;

(c) the declared pair preparations are the images under the inverse regrouping
map of the symmetry-decomposition theorem
([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]]) of the
factored vectors
$$\Psi_{T}:=\Theta^{-1}\bigl(\varphi_-\otimes(e_+\otimes e_+)\bigr),\qquad \Psi_{S}:=\Theta^{-1}\bigl(\varphi_+\otimes\sigma_-\bigr),\qquad \varphi_\pm:=\frac{u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u}{\sqrt2},\quad \sigma_-:=\frac{e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+}{\sqrt2},$$
which are unit vectors of $\mathfrak H_2^-$ by the cited thought experiment.
$\Psi_{T}$ is the parallel-spin (spin-triplet) preparation and $\Psi_{S}$ the
spin-singlet preparation of the declared two-orbital model.

The example computes the declared pair-interaction expectations
$q(\varphi_\pm,\varphi_\pm)$ of the two preparations and shows
that the exchange integral $X$ separates them strictly.

## Verification

**Given:** The declared two-orbital model of the Example: real normalized orthogonal orbitals $u,v\in W^{1,2}\cap L^{2}$, the compressed interaction $A$ defined from $M_W$ with $W=\kappa/|\cdot|$, and the preparations $\Psi_{T},\Psi_{S}$.

[L1] **Sector data.** $\varphi_+$ and $\varphi_-$ are the unit spatial pair vectors of the declared orbitals, and $\Theta^{-1}(\varphi_-\otimes(e_+\otimes e_+))$ and $\Theta^{-1}(\varphi_+\otimes\sigma_-)$ are unit vectors of the antisymmetric two-particle sector, the first a spin-triplet and the second a spin-singlet preparation ([[texp-nrqm-identical-particles-two-fermion-spatial-spin-symmetry]] clauses (a),(c),(d), [[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]] clauses (b),(d)).

[L2] **Slater direct and exchange calculation.** For normalized orthogonal $u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and $W=\kappa/|\cdot|$ with $\kappa>0$, the vectors $\Theta_{6}\varphi_\pm$ lie in $D(M_W)$ and with $D:=\int_{\mathbb R^{6}}|u(x)|^{2}|v(y)|^{2}W(x-y)\,dx\,dy$, $X:=\int_{\mathbb R^{6}}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}W(x-y)\,dx\,dy$ one has $D,X\in\mathbb R$, $0\le D<+\infty$, $X\ge0$ and $\langle M_W\Theta_6\varphi_\pm,\Theta_6\varphi_\pm\rangle=D\pm X$, where $\Theta_6$ is the Euclidean product identification of the spatial tensor square with $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6})$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] clauses (c),(d)).

[L3] **Orthonormality of the spatial combinations.** For orthonormal $u,v$ in a Hilbert space, the vectors $u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u$ over $\sqrt2$ are orthonormal, and $\sigma_-$ is a unit vector ([[lem-nrqm-identical-particles-two-particle-exchange-operator]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (c)).

[L4] **Gaussian-square representation and approximate identity.** The proof of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]], step 2.1, gives for $f=uv\in L^1$ and every $s>0$
$$I_s:=\iint f(x)f(y)e^{-s|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy=(4s/\pi)^{3/2}\|G_{2s}*f\|_2^2\ge0,\qquad X=\kappa\pi^{-1/2}\int_0^\infty s^{-1/2}I_s\,ds,$$
where $G_{2s}(x)=e^{-2s|x|^2}$. In particular the convolution lies in $L^2$ even though no $L^2$ hypothesis on $f$ is used: completing the square makes the absolute triple integral at most $(\pi/(4s))^{3/2}\|f\|_1^2$, and Fubini gives the displayed norm identity ([[thm-gaussian-integral]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]). For a nonnegative integrable function, zero integral implies vanishing a.e. ([[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]]). Normalized dilates of an integrable mass-one kernel converge by convolution to $f$ in $L^1$ ([[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]], Statement and proof steps 1.3, 3.2, 4.1).

[L5] **Compression and tensor expectation.** Translated Hardy gives $\iint|a(x)b(y)|^2/|x-y|^2\,dx\,dy\le4\|a\|_2^2\|\nabla b\|_2^2$ for $a,b\in K$ ([[lem-nrqm-coulomb-three-dimensional-hardy-bound]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]); hence $J(E)\subset D(M_W)$. Cauchy-Schwarz makes $q(z,z')=\langle M_WJz,Jz'\rangle$ finite ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]). The displayed finite matrix defines $A$ on all of $E$; reality of $W$ gives $q(z,z')=\overline{q(z',z)}$, so $A=A^*$, and real orbitals give real entries. Swapping $x,y$ gives $q(\tau_Kz,\tau_Kz')=q(z,z')$, since $W(x-y)=W(y-x)$; thus $A$ commutes with $\tau_K$. The regrouping identity in [L1] now shows that $\Theta^{-1}(A\otimes I)\Theta$ commutes with total exchange and preserves the antisymmetric sector. The bounded tensor construction and its inner-product formula give $\langle(A\otimes I)(\varphi\otimes\chi),\varphi\otimes\chi\rangle=\langle A\varphi,\varphi\rangle\|\chi\|^2=q(\varphi,\varphi)$ for unit $\chi$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

**Proof technique:** direct; normalise the two declared preparations, evaluate the model's interaction expectation through the direct-and-exchange calculation, and prove strict positivity using the Gaussian-square representation and convergence of normalized Gaussian convolutions in $L^1$.

**Given:** The data of the Example and [L1]-[L5].

1.1 [The two preparations are unit vectors] By [L3] the vectors $\varphi_+$ and $\varphi_-$ are orthonormal, and $e_+\otimes e_+$ and $\sigma_-$ are unit vectors of $V\otimes V$; since $\Theta$ is unitary, the vectors $\Psi_{T}=\Theta^{-1}(\varphi_-\otimes(e_+\otimes e_+))$ and $\Psi_{S}=\Theta^{-1}(\varphi_+\otimes\sigma_-)$ are unit vectors of the sector, which is [L1] read in coordinates. [L1, L3, algebra]

1.2 [Strict positivity of the exchange integral] Since the real orbitals belong to $L^2$, Cauchy-Schwarz gives $f:=uv\in L^1$, and $f\ne0$ by hypothesis. If $X=0$, [L4] and the zero-integral criterion imply $I_s=0$ for a.e. $s>0$, because the weight $s^{-1/2}$ is strictly positive. Using the already assumed Countable Choice, choose $s_n\in(n,n+1)$ outside the null exceptional set for each integer $n\ge1$; then $s_n\to\infty$ and the Gaussian-square identity gives $G_{2s_n}*f=0$ in $L^2$, hence a.e. Put $H_s(x):=(2s/\pi)^{3/2}e^{-2s|x|^2}$, a mass-one Gaussian by the Gaussian integral. With $K_0(x):=\pi^{-3/2}e^{-|x|^2}$ and $\varepsilon_s=(2s)^{-1/2}$, one has $H_s(x)=\varepsilon_s^{-3}K_0(x/\varepsilon_s)$; [L4] therefore gives $H_{s_n}*f\to f$ in $L^1$. These convolutions are zero a.e., so $\|f\|_1=0$, a contradiction. Thus $X>0$ and $D-X<D+X$. This uses only $f\in L^1$; the $L^2$ functions are the Gaussian convolutions. [L2, L4, given, choose, algebra]

2.1 [Interaction expectations] By [L5] the declared interaction expectation of a factored preparation $\varphi\otimes\chi$ with unit $\chi$ is $q(\varphi,\varphi)=\langle M_WJ\varphi,J\varphi\rangle$. On the spatial pair vectors $J\varphi_\pm=\Theta_6\varphi_\pm$, so [L2] gives $q(\varphi_+,\varphi_+)=D+X$ and $q(\varphi_-,\varphi_-)=D-X$. Hence the singlet preparation $\Psi_S$ has expectation $D+X$ and the parallel-spin triplet preparation $\Psi_T$ has expectation $D-X$. [L2, L5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Comparison and reading] By steps 2.1 and 1.2 the declared parallel-spin (triplet) preparation has strictly smaller pair-interaction expectation than the singlet preparation in the declared model, the difference being $2X>0$; the terms $D$ and $X$ are the direct and exchange contributions of the calculation [L2], and the pairing of spatial antisymmetry with the triplet is the reading of [L1]. This is the announced computation; no claim about an actual atomic system, no measured energy and no apparatus statement is made. [L1, L2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What "exchange" names.** In this model the name refers to the difference
  $2X$ between the two pair expectations, a property of the declared
  orbitals and interaction; the calculation does not attribute a mechanical
  force to it and does not by itself identify the energy of any atom.
- **Nonzero orbital overlap.** Orthogonality of the real orbitals gives $\int uv=0$; a nonzero product consequently changes sign on sets of positive measure. The Gaussian-square argument proves $X>0$ for every nonzero product, without a sign assumption. If $uv=0$ a.e., then $X=0$ and the pair expectations coincide.
- **Finite orbital model.** The interaction is the compression of the Coulomb form to $K\widehat\otimes K$. The full multiplier need not preserve this finite spatial subspace. The separate maps $\Theta$ and $\Theta_6$ respectively regroup orbital and spin factors and identify spatial tensors with Euclidean wavefunctions.

items.physical_scope: A conditional computation in the declared two-orbital model of two spin-half fermions with a declared Coulomb-form pair interaction: the spatial pair expectations D+X and D-X of the singlet and parallel-spin triplet preparations and the strict positivity of the exchange integral X for nonzero orbital products. The example asserts no atomic physics, no measured energy, no apparatus and no empirical result; the two orbitals and the interaction form are declared idealizations of the model.

items.title: Scope of the identical-particles examples page
items.statement:
## Scope of the examples page

**What the computations establish.** Both items are conditional statements of
declared models. [[texp-nrqm-identical-particles-two-fermion-spatial-spin-symmetry]]
decomposes the antisymmetric two-particle sector of a declared spin-half
species with a finite orbital factor into its spin-singlet and spin-triplet
parts, exhibits the opposite orbital exchange symmetry of the two parts, and
computes the components of an antisymmetrised product of two declared
one-particle states. [[ex-nrqm-identical-particles-exchange-versus-coulomb-terms]]
specialises a two-orbital model with a declared Coulomb-form interaction and
shows, for real normalized orthogonal $W^{1,2}$ orbitals with a nonzero
product, that the declared parallel-spin (triplet)
preparation has strictly smaller pair-interaction expectation than the singlet
preparation, the difference being twice the exchange integral.

**What they rest on.** Both rest on the adopted antisymmetric sector of P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]:
the assignment of the species to the antisymmetric sector and the choice of
orbital factor are model declarations, and in the second item the two orbitals
and the interaction form are declared idealizations. The spin-statistics
association is not derived, no interaction is derived from the sector and no
dynamics is introduced.

**What is not claimed.** The page records no measured energy, no count and no
apparatus response; the terms "singlet", "triplet" and "exchange" name
components and differences of the declared models. Whether a laboratory pair
of particles is described by one of the declared preparations is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]], and agreement of these
conditional numbers with data would test the combined model and apparatus
assumptions rather than prove the model.
